reference_claim: Federal courts have said that same-sex couples may marry, while outdated language in the California Constitution still states that marriage may only be between a man and a woman.
supporting_source_text: The federal courts have said that same-sex couples can marry, but outdated language in the California Constitution still says that marriage can only be between a man and a woman.
importance_note: Explains the mismatch between current federal court rulings and the existing text of the California Constitution.

reference_claim: Proposition 3 amends the California Constitution to recognize a fundamental right to marry regardless of sex or race.
supporting_source_text: • Amends the California Constitution to recognize a fundamental right to marry, regardless of sex or race.
importance_note: States the measure's principal constitutional change and the protected characteristics expressly named by the source.

reference_claim: The measure removes the California Constitution's language limiting marriage to a man and a woman and updates the Constitution to match federal court rulings about who may marry.
supporting_source_text:
• Removes language in the California Constitution stating that marriage is only between a man and a woman.

Proposition 3 updates the Constitution to match what the federal courts have said about who can marry.
importance_note: Captures both the specific obsolete language being removed and the measure's stated alignment function.

reference_claim: Proposition 3 would not change who is currently allowed to marry in California.
supporting_source_text: Proposition 3 would not change who is allowed to marry in California.
importance_note: Clarifies that the amendment changes constitutional text without changing present marriage eligibility.

reference_claim: The measure would cause no change in revenues or costs for state or local governments.
supporting_source_text: This means there would be no change in revenues or costs to state and local governments.
importance_note: Records the official conclusion that the measure has no state or local government fiscal effect.
